model_annotation: Figure 10 presents a matrix illustrating the effect of TARG and PERMUTE on the degree of perturbation observed during morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models. The horizontal axis, labeled “Language Family,” displays a linear scale with categories representing various language families including Dravidian, Germanic, Romance, Slavic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “Perturbation,” also utilizes a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.1. The matrix consists of rows representing the perturbation models TARG and PERMUTE, and columns representing the language families. The cells within the matrix contain numerical values representing the magnitude of the perturbation effect for each combination of model and language family.  The largest value in the matrix, located in the PERMUTE column for the Romance language family, is approximately 0.20, while the smallest value, found in the TARG column for the Uralic language family, is approximately 0.01.  The bars are not sorted, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their relative heights within the matrix.
